Some of the biggest government scholarships in the world never ask for it; others accept a free letter from your university instead, and a growing group takes cheaper tests you can sit from home. What you should not believe is any list that names twenty scholarships as “no IELTS” without explaining the catch, because there usually is one: a scholarship not requiring IELTS is not the same as the university not requiring proof of English. In this article, we have explained the three real routes to studying abroad without IELTS, which fully funded scholarships use each route, and how to prove your English the free way.
